# arthron

> A fetch client assembled from plugins. Returns native `Response`; middleware controls flow (can retry via `next`), interceptors transform values. Zero dependencies, ESM + CJS, Node 22+ and browsers, TypeScript 5.0+.

Import: `import { arthron, isArthronError, SchemaError, definePlugin } from "arthron";` and the built-in plugins `import { bearerAuth, retry, timeout, logging, uploadProgress } from "arthron/plugins";` (only there — not from "arthron").

## Create

```ts
const api = arthron({
  baseURL?: string,              // prefix for relative paths; required unless you pass absolute URLs
  allowAbsoluteUrls?: boolean,   // default false: an absolute URL must stay on baseURL's origin
  headers?: HeadersInit,         // defaults, per-call headers win (case-insensitive); { name: null } in extend/per-call drops one
  credentials?, cache?, redirect?, mode?, keepalive?, …  // any fetch option (RequestInit minus body/method/headers/signal/window) as a default; per-call wins; NOT set unless you set it; passing signal/body/method throws
  fetch?: typeof fetch,          // injection for tests/polyfills, resolved per request
  use?: Plugin[],                // plugins, outermost first
  errorDetail?: (data: unknown, res: Response) => string | undefined, // picks ArthronError.detail
  throwOn?: (res: Response) => boolean, // which non-ok responses reject; also a per-call option
});
```

## Request

```ts
api.get(path, init?) | api.delete(path, init?) | api.head(path, init?)
api.post(path, body?, init?) | api.put(path, body?, init?) | api.patch(path, body?, init?) | api.query(path, body?, init?)   // QUERY = RFC 10008
api.request(path, { method, body?, ...init })      // method: HttpMethod (GET…QUERY autocomplete, any string allowed); standard ones sent uppercased
// init = RequestInit minus method/body, plus params?: Record<string, scalar | scalar[] | null | undefined> | URLSearchParams (arrays → repeated keys; object values → TypeError); headers values may be null to drop a default; meta?: ArthronMeta (plugin settings, not sent); path?: Record<string, string|number> fills {name} placeholders, encoded per segment ("", ".", ".." refused) — use it instead of interpolating ids
```

Every method returns `Promise<Response>` plus helpers:
`.json<T>()` (cast) / `.json(schema)` (any Standard Schema — Zod, Valibot, ArkType; typed from it; mismatch → SchemaError with .issues, not an ArthronError) `.text()` `.blob()` `.arrayBuffer()` `.formData()` `.sse({ maxLineLength?, maxEventSize? }?): AsyncIterable<{event?,data,id?,lastEventId,retry?}> (lastEventId and retry persist across events, per spec; no reconnection)` `.ndjson<T>({ maxLineLength? }?): AsyncIterable<T>` — limits default to 8 Mi characters; exceeding one rejects with RangeError and cancels the body

- Body: string/FormData/Blob/ArrayBuffer/URLSearchParams/ReadableStream sent as-is (matched by type tag, so polyfill/cross-realm instances count; streams get `duplex: "half"`; FormData is sent without content-type so the runtime sets the boundary). Any other value (incl. null) → JSON + `content-type: application/json`; a content type you set must be JSON-ish (else TypeError). Map/Set/iterables/async iterables (Node streams)/functions → TypeError. GET/HEAD with body → TypeError.
- URL: `baseURL` + path by string concatenation (`"https://a/v1" + "/u"` → `https://a/v1/u`). An absolute path must be http(s) and, when baseURL is set, on baseURL's origin — else TypeError, unless `allowAbsoluteUrls: true`; config headers are never sent to another origin. On cross-origin redirects fetch drops Authorization but keeps custom headers (x-api-key) — use `redirect: "error"` where that matters. `params` appended with `&` if a query exists, placed before `#fragment`.
- Argument errors (no baseURL, URL the global fetch cannot parse, BigInt body, missing method) reject the promise with TypeError before fetch; they do not throw synchronously and are never retried. URLs are pre-checked only for the global fetch; an injected `fetch` decides its own URL rules (relative URLs are fine if it accepts them).
- `.sse()`/`.ndjson()`: leaving the loop early cancels the body. `.sse()` drops an event the stream ends inside (spec).

## Errors

```ts
class ArthronError extends Error {
  status: number;        // HTTP status, 0 = network failure
  statusText: string;
  headers: Headers;      // not enumerable
  message: string;       // arthron's: "GET https://api.test/users/1 failed with 404 Not Found" / "… failed: fetch failed" — no query, no server text
  detail?: string;       // the server's explanation (body message → error → error.message → detail); untrusted — show as text
  data: unknown;         // JSON if parseable, else text, else undefined; from at most 64 KiB of body (text if cut)
  response?: Response;   // still readable, holding what was read (≤ 64 KiB); absent for network failure; not enumerable
  request: { url: string; init: RequestInit }; // not enumerable (holds credentials)
  cause?: unknown;       // underlying error for network failure
  toJSON(): { name, message, detail, status, statusText, method, url /* no query/userinfo */, data };
}
isArthronError(e): e is ArthronError   // branded with Symbol.for: works (and instanceof works) across the ESM and CJS copies
```

- Only `!response.ok` and fetch rejection become ArthronError — and not every non-ok: opaque responses (no-cors) and the 3xx of `redirect: "manual"` are returned; `throwOn(res)` (config or per call) narrows further. An ok response never rejects. Aborts (`AbortError`/`TimeoutError` or any custom `abort(reason)`, including during the error-body read) and exceptions thrown by plugins propagate untouched and skip error interceptors.
- Serializing an ArthronError (JSON.stringify, console.error, error trackers, logging onEvent) never includes request headers, body, query or userinfo. Error messages arthron writes leave the query out too.
- `message` is arthron's (for logs); `detail` is the server's (for UI: `e.detail ?? fallback`). Default `detail`: body `message` → `error` (string) → `error.message` → `detail`, else undefined. Override with `errorDetail`.

## Plugins

```ts
type Plugin = {
  name?: string;   // identity: use/extend replace a same-named plugin in place; without(name) removes it
  middleware?: (ctx, next: (ctx) => Promise<Response>) => Promise<Response>; // wraps the call; may call next again (retry) or not at all
  request?: (ctx) => ctx;                      // per attempt, before fetch
  response?: (res, ctx) => Response;           // per successful attempt; body is single-use, clone() to peek
  error?: (err: ArthronError, ctx) => ArthronError; // per failed attempt; return value is always thrown
};
type RequestContext = { url: string; init: Omit<RequestInit, "headers"> & { headers: Record<string, string> }; meta: ArthronMeta; adapter?: typeof fetch }; // adapter: the function this attempt is sent with (client's, else global) — a plugin may replace or wrap it per attempt; send still makes every ArthronError. headers: lowercase record, re-normalized after each request interceptor — spreading is safe
// meta: per-call plugin settings from api.get(path, { meta }), never sent. Built-ins read meta.bearerAuth (false), meta.onUploadProgress (callback), meta.retry (false | options) and meta.timeout (ms).
// Add keys: declare module "arthron" { interface ArthronMeta { skipTrace?: boolean } }
```

Order: `middleware[0]( middleware[1]( attempt: request interceptors → fetch → response | error interceptors ) )` — a middleware is called once; code after `await next(ctx)` runs after the response interceptors. Inside `try`, write `return await next(ctx)` or the catch misses the error. Default order: `[logging(), bearerAuth(…), timeout(ms), retry()]` (timeout before retry = whole call, after = per attempt). Same-named plugins replace each other; for two timeouts rename one: `{ ...timeout(30_000), name: "callTimeout" }`. Values that must be fresh per attempt (token, signature) → request interceptor; the same on every attempt (idempotency key) → middleware before retry. Each attempt gets a fresh copy of ctx (headers, and a FormData/URLSearchParams body).

`api.use(...plugins)`, `api.extend(config)` and `api.without(...names)` return NEW clients; the original is unchanged. A named plugin replaces the one with the same name at its position (built-ins: "bearerAuth", "retry", "timeout", "logging", "uploadProgress"); unnamed plugins append.

Helpers (identity, for typing): `definePlugin(p)`, `defineMiddleware(m)`, `defineInterceptor.request(f) / .response(f) / .error(f)`.

## Built-in plugins (from "arthron/plugins")

- `retry({ retries=2, retryOn=[408,429,500,502,503,504], methods=[GET,HEAD,OPTIONS,QUERY,PUT,DELETE], delay=(n)=>Math.random()*300*2**n /* full jitter */, maxRetryAfter=60000, shouldRetry?(error, attempt, ctx) → true|false|undefined, onRetry?(error, attempt, waitMs) })` — re-runs the whole attempt (request interceptors included). Honours Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date). Never retries ReadableStream bodies or aborted requests, nor beyond `retries`; by default never non-ArthronErrors (shouldRetry may opt in, e.g. an inner TimeoutError). With methods: ["POST"], network errors (status 0) are retried too — refuse them with shouldRetry where a duplicate would hurt. Per call: `meta: { retry: false }` or `meta: { retry: { retries: 5 } }`. `retries` must be a whole number ≥ 0 (TypeError otherwise); waits are capped at 2^31-1 ms.
- `timeout(ms)` | `timeout({ total?, idle? })` — `total` (= `ms`): deadline from attempt start until the body is fully read; `idle`: aborts after that many ms without data (headers or chunks), so `timeout({ idle: 30_000 })` never cuts a flowing stream. Both together: whichever trips first. `{}` → TypeError; so is a second argument (the 1.x `timeout(ms, { idle })`). Rejects with TimeoutError (not ArthronError; retry ignores it). Place after `retry` for per-attempt, before it for total. Per call: `meta: { timeout: ms }` (Infinity lifts it). `Infinity` = no deadline; NaN/negative/>2^31-1 → TypeError. Keeps `res.url`/`redirected`/`type` (through `clone()` too); timers are unref'd.
- `bearerAuth({ origin, token, refresh? })` — `authorization: Bearer <token>` on every attempt, only to requests on `origin` (a URL or array; only origins count, non-http(s) → TypeError). `token: () => string | null | undefined | Promise<…>`, read per attempt; empty → no header. With `refresh: () => Promise<void>`, a 401 refreshes and redoes the call once: concurrent 401s share one refresh, a call whose token was already replaced retries without refreshing, a second 401 is thrown, a rejected refresh reaches every waiting call unchanged. Without `refresh`, or for a ReadableStream body (cannot be resent), 401 is thrown without refreshing. Per call: `meta: { bearerAuth: false }` = no token, no refresh — required on the login/refresh requests if they use the same client (else the refresh's own 401 waits on itself). Token is opaque: refresh ahead of a JWT's exp inside `token()`.
- `logging({ enabled=true, logger=console, onEvent?, now? })` — start/success/error lines or structured events `{ phase, method, path, status?, ms?, error? }`. Never prints query strings or userinfo. Does not log cancellations.
- `uploadProgress()` — does nothing alone; a call with `meta: { onUploadProgress: ({ loaded, total, progress }) => … }` and a body reports upload progress (total/progress undefined when the size is unknown; restarts at 0 per attempt; no events after the response or an abort). Browser (incl. Electron renderer): sent over XMLHttpRequest (cross-origin → CORS preflight; response not streamed; redirect "manual"/"error", mode "no-cors", credentials "omit" to the page's origin → TypeError before sending; cache/priority/referrerPolicy/integrity/keepalive ignored; ReadableStream body → no progress). Node (incl. jsdom on Node): fetch with the body counted in ≤ 64 KiB steps, content-length and Blob content-type kept (S3 presigned PUT works); FormData encoded with a known length, files streamed. Deno/Bun/Cloudflare Workers/Electron main/service workers, an injected fetch or another transport plugin → sent as usual without progress. A throwing callback rejects the call with its own error (not ArthronError, not retried) — keep uploadProgress last in use. Works through ctx.adapter.

## Recipes

Auth refresh — built in (`bearerAuth()` above; examples/auth-refresh.ts). The refresh request skips auth:
```ts
const api = arthron({ baseURL: API, use: [bearerAuth({ origin: API, token: () => tok, refresh: async () => {
  tok = (await api.post("/token/refresh", undefined, { meta: { bearerAuth: false } }).json<{ access_token: string }>()).access_token;
} })] });
```

Reacting to a call's final outcome (error page, domain error) is middleware registered BEFORE retry() — error interceptors run per attempt, including attempts a retry then recovers (see examples/error-page.ts).

Streaming an LLM response:
```ts
for await (const { data } of api.post("/v1/chat/completions", { model, messages, stream: true }).sse()) {
  if (data === "[DONE]") break;          // provider sentinel, not handled by arthron
  const chunk = JSON.parse(data);
}
```

## Non-goals

No request/response key transformation, no caching, no dedupe, no backend-envelope unwrapping. Do those in your adapter layer.

## Types

Public object types are interfaces (ArthronConfig, RequestOptions, RequestInitWithBody, RequestContext, ArthronMeta, Plugin, ArthronPromise, Arthron): extend them with `declare module "arthron" { interface … }`.
